summary: Preserved PR 679's valid ISA analyzer and parser fixes, reproduced PR 683's exact YAML metadata counterexample on candidate b0d6d33d6256a013e0a5ba4a4f0a5308998ee954, and excluded .amdgpu_metadata YAML payloads from instruction and family counts. The retained gfx950 sample now reports 28 instructions instead of 35.

tests.what_was_measured: Failing-before reproduction: 35 instructions, including seven YAML scalar values misclassified as opcodes, versus 28 actual instructions.
Passing-after real compiler ISA analysis: exactly 28 instructions and no YAML values in the opcode table.
32 tests passed and 2 environment-dependent tests skipped; covers YAML metadata, prior comment/label fixes, compiler hints, and external LLVM codegen compatibility.
Two gfx950 tests passed, including optimized GPU output agreement with the portable GPU reference and final-ISA generation/shape assertions.

gpu_execution_evidence: Two tests passed on the assigned AMD Instinct MI355X (gfx950); one compares optimized execution with a portable GPU reference and the other asserts compiler-emitted final ISA properties.
remaining_limitations: Physical VGPR/SGPR pinning or named register-region reservation remains unimplemented.
Exact hand-scheduled region preservation and MFMA co-execute-window assertions remain unimplemented.
The requested first-class AMD instruction helpers remain unimplemented.
The requested exact low-level buffer load/store API remains unimplemented.
The requested compiler-option sweep example remains unimplemented.
Static ISA analysis does not prove scheduling guarantees, physical register placement, cycle timing, dependency correctness, occupancy, or handwritten-kernel performance parity.
Only gfx950 hardware was available; other CDNA and RDNA architectures were not tested.
No native rebuild was performed because this correction changes only Python, tests, documentation, and reports.
